description: Replace one-vertex split decomposition with orbit-balanced adjacent- or nonadjacent-pair anchors. The hypothesis is that a stronger case partition shrinks the exact residue more than a stronger solver on the old partition.
mathematical_formalization: Choose anchor pair (u,v) modulo automorphism orbits and decompose partial colorings by the joint neighborhood signature sigma(u,v) instead of sigma(v) alone.
implementation_hypothesis: Benchmark adjacent and nonadjacent anchor pairs under the same proof-logging pipeline used by the split/gluing baseline.
experiment_seed: Compare residue size and proof bytes for one-vertex vs pair-split decomposition on solved ladder rungs.

closest_prior_art.title: A new upper bound on the Ramsey number R(5,5)

novelty_claim: The decomposition primitive changes, not just the engine underneath it.
differentiation: If the primitive does not improve residue or checker cost, this route is killed.
